survey: A cartoon steam locomotive on desert track, seen from the front-left at three-quarter view. The front is the round smokebox face of a horizontal boiler that rests on a flat running board. On top of the boiler sit a flared smokestack with a headlamp on its front, a steam dome and a brass bell. A boxy cab with windows and a round porthole joins the rear of the boiler, and a coal-filled tender is coupled behind the cab. Under the running board, from front to back, are a red buffer beam with a slatted cowcatcher, one small red pilot wheel, a cylinder whose piston rod drives a crosshead, three large red driving wheels, and two small trailing or tender wheels. All the wheels sit on the near rail. The rods run from the crosshead to the driving wheels.

errors.where: Side rods on the driving wheels
errors.what: The running gear could not turn the wheels. Two separate rods leave the crosshead. One goes to a crank pin on the first driver. The other pins straight onto the hubs (axle centres) of the second and third drivers, not onto offset crank pins. A rod fixed at the axle centres cannot transmit motion, and nothing couples the first driver to the other two.

errors.where: Cowcatcher (pilot) under the red buffer beam
errors.what: The bottom ends of the pilot bars reach right down onto the rails and ties. A real pilot has clearance above the track, so this one would drag along the rails and catch on the sleepers.

fix: Single connected running gear: the piston rod drives a crosshead, one main rod runs from the crosshead to an offset crank pin on a driving wheel, and one coupling rod links offset crank pins on all three driving wheels, set away from the wheel hubs. Cowcatcher bars end a little above the rails, with a clear gap between the pilot and the track.
